html:
The Balts are the peoples of the eastern Baltic coast who speak Baltic languages. On the map for 700 they hold the lands of today's Lithuania, Latvia and parts of Belarus and Russia.

In these centuries they were many separate tribes: the Old Prussians, Curonians, Semigallians, Latgalians, Lithuanians and Yotvingians among them. They farmed, kept cattle and lived in wooden hillforts. They traded amber from their coast south along the Amber Road and kept their own gods long after their neighbours became Christian.

The Baltic tribes held out until the Northern Crusades of the 1200s, when German knights conquered the Prussians and Latvians. The Lithuanians alone built a large state, Lithuania, which stayed pagan until 1387. Only Lithuanian and Latvian survive today.
sum: The Balts are the peoples of the eastern Baltic coast who speak Baltic languages. On the map for 700 they hold the lands of today's Lithuania, Latvia and parts of Belarus and Russia.
